To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a predictive coding model of speech acquisition can be used to learn temporal patterns among primitive vocalizations and control the vocal tract to produce the learned patterns.
a predictive coding model of speech acquisition learns to vocalize and control the motor system in a more efficient manner.
a model that minimizes sensory and proprioceptive prediction error can learn temporal vocalization patterns and can compute control for effective vocalization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emergence of vocal developmental sequences in a predictive coding model of speech acquisition.
the development of a computational model that is capable of learning temporal patterns and motor control of vocalization.
the emergence of vocal development sequences from primitive speech sounds and the learning of vocal control/muscle activations in a predictive coding framework.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this model is a step in the right direction towards a more complete and biologically plausible model of speech learning and production.
our proposed predictive coding framework is able to learn the control/muscles activation for the learned syllables and the model outperforms the other existing models in the literature.
the predictive coding framework can be used to explain the emergence of speech developmental sequences in the infant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the model can learn to vocalize a syllable by minimizing its sensory prediction error, while it can learn to control its motor apparatus to produce the syllable by minimizing the proprioceptive prediction error.
the model learns to vocalize and control the vocal apparatus simultaneously.
the model learns temporal patterns and control simultaneously and in a unified framework.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single objective can be used to learn both temporal patterns and control.
the model learns vocal sequences in a manner that is similar to the emergence of developmental sequences in infants, and that the model is able to learn vocalization classes with minimal supervision.
the model learns the temporal structure of speech sequences and the control for effective production of these sequences simultaneously, without any explicit learning or tuning of the control.
